comments.body:
═══ ARCHAEOLOGY SETTLES IT: Pass-1 DID generate findings on OPUS until 2026-06-27, and the downgrade
to sonnet is a five-week-old REGRESSION — not a design choice. This reframes the fix entirely. ═══

I previously wrote on this ticket that the mitigation was to raise the rung from `trivial` to
`standard`, on the reasoning that sonnet was "where it runs today". **That was wrong.** Sonnet is
itself the result of an unnoticed regression, so preserving it would ratify the bug. Corrected below
with the evidence.

**THE EMPIRICAL RECORD.** 3,843 plan-review `REVIEW_RESULT` sidecars in `.tickets-tracker`, aggregated
by the recorded `data.model`, bucketed by day:

    day           opus   sonnet
    2026-06-24      16        0
    2026-06-25      32        0
    2026-06-26      25        0
    2026-06-27      42        0     <- `_verifier_cfg` lands this day
    2026-06-28      37       20     <- transition
    2026-06-29       0       87     <- opus GONE
    2026-06-30       0       78
    ...              0      ...     (never returns; 2,710 sonnet runs since)

115 opus runs before the change, ZERO after. A total, permanent changeover one day after the commit.

**THE CAUSE.** `4beec08a4` (2026-06-27, "verifier model downgrade in the workflow path", WS2
gawky-koi-grain) introduced `_verifier_cfg` to run **Pass-2 verify and Pass-4 coach** on the decisive
non-frontier model. Its own docstring asserts: *"The Pass-1 finder is unaffected: it runs the YAML
`model_ladder` via the ProductionBatchRunner, not `cfg.model`."*

That claim was false from the moment it was written, for a reason nobody could see at the time:
`_verifier_cfg(cfg)` is passed as the **whole run's** cfg at the `produce_plan_review_verdict`
boundary (`plan_review/__init__.py:605-607`), so `gate_dispatch` builds the RUNNER from the
downgraded cfg — and `PydanticAIRunner.run` then **discarded `req.config`**, throwing away the batch's
ladder rung and using the runner's downgraded config instead. So Pass-1 silently inherited a downgrade
aimed at Pass-2/Pass-4.

**WHAT THIS MEANS FOR b690 — it is the ENABLER, not the cause.** Without b690, NO ladder rung can
influence Pass-1 at all, because `req.config` is discarded before it is read. b690 is what makes the
declaration reachable for the first time. The remaining problem is only that the declaration says
`trivial`.

**SO THE FIX IS A RESTORATION, and the correct rung is `frontier`:**

    b690 (honour req.config)  +  plan-review.yaml model_ladder[0] = frontier
      => Pass-1 generates findings on opus, as it did before 2026-06-27
      => and `_verifier_cfg`'s docstring claim finally becomes TRUE

`standard` would freeze the regression. `trivial` would deepen it. Only `frontier` restores the
behaviour that produced 115 recorded reviews, and it is the only option that is a preservation rather
than a new judgement about how strong a finder should be.

**A SEPARATE UNTHREADED SEAM, found in the same trace and NOT covered by this ticket or by 7761.**
`sizing.MODEL_LADDER` still hardcodes BARE Anthropic ids (`claude-haiku-4-5` 200k /
`claude-sonnet-4-6` 1M / `claude-opus-4-8` 1M), and `models_at_or_above` returns them, so
`sizing.py:424` does `replace(cfg, model=<bare claude-* id>)` on every context-limit escalation.
**Escalation therefore bypasses the model-class table entirely** — on a Bedrock-configured run, an
escalating Pass-1 criterion silently jumps to direct Anthropic. That is the same defect class as the
epic's founding symptom (41 of 42 calls to direct Anthropic) and it is still live. Filing separately.

Also worth noting for whoever sets the rung: with rung 0 at `frontier`, `models_at_or_above(opus)`
returns just `[opus]`, so escalation becomes a no-op — which costs nothing, because sonnet and opus
have the SAME 1M window. The only size-meaningful step in that ladder was ever haiku→sonnet, and the
genuinely useful size handling (batch → one-criterion-per-call → the P8 too-big finding) is
independent of the model rungs.

MISSING TEST: DONE. ATTESTATION: recipe below, not yet satisfied.

## The absent test now exists
Commit 14a98e02ac on branch test/77ed-prereq-window in /Users/joeoakhart/rebar-wt-77ed (stacked, nothing
amended; NOT pushed — it predates the stack landing and needs a rebase onto current origin/main first).

Assertion: tests/unit/test_pass1_finder_model.py:187, in
test_the_prerequisite_finder_packs_against_the_frontier_model (from :150).

The gap was REAL and was confirmed independently: every pre-existing site monkeypatched
largest_window_tokens to a synthetic number (test_plan_review_prerequisites.py:59,203;
test_plan_review_prerequisites_heldout.py:73), test_plan_review_prerequisites_model_log.py:42 stubbed
pack_prerequisite_bins out entirely, and test_pass1_finder_model.py never exercised the prerequisite arm
(its _entry_model helper passed no with_inputs, so run_focused_finder was never reached).

WIRING IS CORRECT — no production defect. production_batch_runner.py resolves
cfg.model = resolve_model_string(model_ladder[0]) (the shipped YAML's frontier) before calling
run_focused_finder, which forwards model=cfg.model into pack_prerequisite_bins at prerequisites.py:187.

The test discriminates for real: a helper retargets ONLY the frontier slot to
bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8 so it differs from the default cfg.model, with a guard that fails
loudly if that ever collapses. largest_window_tokens is deliberately left UNPATCHED — the observable is
the model string, not a window number. That matters because ticket 1157 means sonnet and opus both
declare 1_000_000, so a window assertion would pass for the wrong reason.

MUTATION-CHECKED BOTH DIRECTIONS, then restored:
  A) prerequisite finder handed the unresolved gate cfg -> FAILED ('packed against claude-opus-4-8')
  B) model=cfg.model -> model=None in prerequisites.py  -> FAILED ('packed against None')
Gates: full default selection EXIT 0 (8876 passed, 31 skipped), make lint EXIT 0, make typecheck EXIT 0.

## The remaining criterion, and exactly how to satisfy it
The AC wants a real plan-review run after the change recording opus for the Pass-1 finder, cited from
REBAR_USAGE_LOG per-step attribution.

WHY IT IS STILL OPEN: the usage log is OPT-IN. usage_log.py:29 ENV_VAR = 'REBAR_USAGE_LOG', and
:269 records only when that var points at a path. A plan-review run was executed on 0d76 during this
session WITHOUT the var set, so it produced no per-step attribution and CANNOT be cited here.

RECIPE (one run satisfies this AND 7a79's cache criterion):
  export REBAR_USAGE_LOG=/tmp/rebar_usage_77ed.jsonl
  rebar review-plan <any unblocked ticket>
then read the JSONL and cite the Pass-1 finder row's model plus the run's aggregate
cache_write_tokens. Record the file path, the row, and a timestamp on the ticket.

OPERATIONAL NOTE from the implementing agent: committing in that worktree required RUFF_CACHE_DIR
pointed OUTSIDE the repo — the pre-commit hook's bare ruff otherwise writes .ruff_cache into the
worktree root and races the repo-leak guard if a suite is running concurrently. Two suite runs reported
exit 1 for that reason and for a commit landing mid-run; neither was a code failure.

The AC asked for a real plan-review run, after the fix, recording opus for the Pass-1 finder, cited

THE RUN

PER-STEP ATTRIBUTION, aggregated from that log by (step, model_class, model):
  5 x (finders,            frontier, anthropic:claude-opus-4-8)   <- Pass-1 FINDER on OPUS
  1 x (verify,             -,        anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6) <- Pass-2

This is the restoration this ticket argued for, observed end-to-end: Pass-1 resolves the declared
frontier class to opus while Pass-2/Pass-4 stay on the standard model — the operator decision
recorded on this epic, and the behaviour the sidecar archaeology showed had been absent since
2026-06-27. The verdict envelope independently reports model=anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6 as the RUN
cfg, which is the point: the finder no longer inherits it. Before b690 the finder would have taken
that sonnet cfg, which is exactly the regression.

The discrimination is real, not incidental: had req.config still been discarded, every row would
carry the run cfg (sonnet) rather than opus, because the run cfg IS sonnet here.

ALSO SATISFIED THIS RUN: the prerequisite-window test criterion. Commit cherry-picked onto current
origin/main (its original parents were SHA-rewritten by Gerrit on submit, so a cherry-pick, not a
rebase); 6 passed in test_pass1_finder_model.py. Re-mutation-checked ON THIS TREE rather than relying
on the pre-merge proof: forcing model=None at prerequisites.py:187 turns
test_the_prerequisite_finder_packs_against_the_frontier_model RED ("packed against None"); restoring
returns it GREEN.

compiled_state.description:
# The pass that GENERATES blocking findings moves to the cheapest model the moment b690 lands

## Severity framing

This is not a cost or consistency issue. **Pass-1 of plan-review is the finder** — it produces the
findings that become blocking and gate every `claim`. Moving it to a weaker model makes the gate
QUIETLY MORE PERMISSIVE, and there is no alarm for "the review was weaker than it should have been".
`b690`'s change is `LLM-Review +1 / Verified +1` and green on every offline test, because **none of
this risk is test-detectable**: the offline suite substitutes `FunctionModel`/`FakeRunner` for exactly
the thing that changes, which is WHICH MODEL a live gate calls.

## The mechanism, verified end to end

Under this repo's actual config there is **no `model_classes` table anywhere** (no `[llm]` in
`rebar.toml`, no `[tool.rebar…]` LLM keys in `pyproject.toml`, no `.rebar/config.conf`, no
`REBAR_LLM_*` in shell rc / LaunchAgents / CI), so classes take built-in defaults:

    trivial -> anthropic:claude-haiku-4-5   standard -> anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6
    frontier -> anthropic:claude-opus-4-8   LLMConfig.from_env().model -> claude-opus-4-8

**Crucially, plan-review's runner floor is NOT `cfg.model`.** `plan_review/__init__.py:609` calls
`produce_plan_review_verdict(ctx, _verifier_cfg(cfg), …)`, so the whole run's
`runner._config.model` is `anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6`. Then:

1. `gate_dispatch.py:163` builds `ProductionBatchRunner(runner=get_runner(_verifier_cfg(cfg)))`
   → floor = sonnet.
2. `production_batch_runner.run` does `cfg = replace(cfg, model=resolve_model_string(req.model_ladder[0]))`
   → `plan-review.yaml:62-65` rung 0 is `trivial` → **haiku**.
3. `pass1.py:484` → `sizing.pass1_with_ladder` → `passes.pass1_chunk` builds
   `RunRequest(..., config=cfg)` (`passes.py:319-330`).
4. **PRE-b690** the runner opened `cfg = self._config` and DISCARDED `req.config` → Pass-1 actually
   ran on **sonnet**. **POST-b690** it honours the declaration and runs on **haiku**.

Measured:

    gate runner floor model  : anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6
    Pass-1 batch cfg.model   : anthropic:claude-haiku-4-5
    PRE-b690  effective model: anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6
    POST-b690 effective model: anthropic:claude-haiku-4-5

**The smoking gun that this was never intended-and-tested:** `origin/main`'s own `_verifier_cfg`
docstring asserts "The Pass-1 finder is unaffected: it runs the YAML `model_ladder` via the
ProductionBatchRunner, not `cfg.model`." **That comment is FALSE on main**, and `b690` is what makes
it true. `git log -L62,66` on `plan-review.yaml` shows Pass-1 has declared the cheapest rung since the
workflow was born (originally the literal `claude-haiku-4-5`) and has **never once actually run on it**.

## Why the ladder does not save it

`pass1_with_ladder` escalates on a **context-limit signal** — it is a SIZE ladder, not a quality
ladder (its own docstring says so). A plan that fits haiku's 200k window stays on haiku forever. Some
Pass-1 chunks also run `execution_mode="agentic"` (code-grounding with tool calls), where the drop
from sonnet to haiku is a large capability change, not a marginal one.

Secondary effect on the prerequisite finder (`registry.py:361-367` gives it
`"default_posture": "blocking"`): `pack_prerequisite_bins(..., model=cfg.model)` now packs for haiku's
200k instead of sonnet's 1M, so context-limit escalation genuinely fires where it previously could
not. Escalation does work (`models_at_or_above('claude-haiku-4-5')` →
`['claude-haiku-4-5','claude-sonnet-4-6','claude-opus-4-8']`), but the first attempt is a real
downgrade and every attempt burns tokens.

## Why it is silent rather than loud

The gates fail CLOSED on errors — `attest_gate.py:112-125` blocks a claim on a missing/stale
attestation, and an LLM outage degrades to INDETERMINATE → no signature → claim blocked. That is the
loud path and it is fine. **This is the other kind:** a haiku Pass-1 that surfaces fewer grounded
findings yields a **PASS**, which gets signed, and the claim proceeds. The sidecar records only the
VERIFIER's model (`data.model`), never Pass-1's, so it is invisible in the artifacts too.

## An asymmetry worth deciding on

Code-review's Pass-1 finder declares **`frontier`** (`code-review.yaml`, landed by 3768). Plan-review's
Pass-1 declares **`trivial`**. Both are finders that generate blocking findings. That asymmetry may be
deliberate, but it has never been effective, so it has never been evaluated.

## The decision, made by the operator and confirmed by archaeology

**Pass-1 (the finder) runs on `frontier`/opus. Pass-2 verify and Pass-4 coach run on
`standard`/sonnet.** That split is what `_verifier_cfg` was written to express, and its own docstring
already asserts it ("The Pass-1 finder is unaffected"). The docstring has simply been false since
2026-06-27.

This is a RESTORATION, not a new preference. The sidecar record shows 115 plan reviews generating
findings on opus up to 2026-06-27, then zero ever since — a total changeover one day after
`4beec08a4` introduced the verifier downgrade and accidentally applied it to the whole run. See the
archaeology comment for the day-by-day table.

**b690 is the ENABLER.** Until it landed, `PydanticAIRunner.run` discarded `req.config`, so NO ladder
rung could influence Pass-1 at all. With b690, the declaration is finally reachable — and it says
`trivial`, which is why the regression would deepen rather than heal on its own.

**The change:** `plan-review.yaml`'s `model_ladder` entry rung `trivial` -> `frontier`.
`standard` would freeze the regression; `trivial` would deepen it.

Note that with rung 0 at `frontier`, `models_at_or_above(opus)` returns just `[opus]`, so model
escalation becomes a no-op. That costs nothing: sonnet and opus share the same 1M window, so the only
size-meaningful step was ever haiku->sonnet, and the size handling that matters (batch ->
one-criterion-per-call -> the P8 too-big finding) is independent of the model rungs.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `plan-review.yaml`'s Pass-1 `model_ladder` entry rung is `frontier`, so findings generate on
      opus as they did before 2026-06-27
- [ ] Pass-2 verify and Pass-4 coach remain on the verifier model (`standard`/sonnet) — this ticket
      must not disturb the downgrade that `_verifier_cfg` correctly applies to them
- [ ] a test asserts the EFFECTIVE model of Pass-1 at the seam that decides it
      (`ProductionBatchRunner` -> `run_pass1` -> `pass1_chunk`, i.e. the model reaching the runner),
      so a future change cannot silently move the finder again. Asserting the YAML text is NOT
      sufficient — the YAML has said `trivial` for five weeks while sonnet actually ran
- [ ] a test asserts Pass-1 and Pass-2 resolve to DIFFERENT models under the default config, since
      the defect was precisely the two collapsing onto one
- [ ] `_verifier_cfg`'s docstring claim that "the Pass-1 finder is unaffected" is either true after
      this change or corrected — it must not remain a false assertion in the code
- [ ] [operator-attested] a real plan-review run after the change records opus for the Pass-1 finder,
      cited from `REBAR_USAGE_LOG` per-step attribution (which story b690 made possible)
- [ ] the prerequisite finder's bin packing is checked against opus's window, since
      `pack_prerequisite_bins` sizes to `cfg.model`

## Notes

Found by an independent landing-safety assessment of the epic stack, NOT by the offline suite — which
is green at the stack tip and cannot see this. `b690` itself is closed and correct in its own terms:
it made declarations effective. This ticket is about one declaration that turns out to be wrong.

file_impact.reason: the Pass-1 model_ladder entry rung: trivial -> frontier
_verifier_cfg docstring asserts the Pass-1 finder is unaffected; false since 2026-06-27, must become true or be corrected
effective-model assertion at the ProductionBatchRunner -> pass1_chunk seam, plus Pass-1 != Pass-2

compiled_state.title: b690 silently downgrades the plan-review Pass-1 finder from sonnet to haiku, weakening the claim gate that generates blocking findings
